I will keep my farm in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because in Quzhou County that is still the most reliable way for me to use the full year, match local water and heat conditions, and protect my income. At my age, I want a system I know well, can mechanize easily, and can manage with fewer surprises. Since my education level is high, I will use improved varieties, soil-testing habits, and tighter fertilizer control instead of chasing complicated diversification. I will keep inputs moderate, not excessive, because grain margins are tight and I care about stable yield more than maximum yield on paper. For wheat, I will focus on strong seedlings, one solid basal fertilizer program, timely spring nitrogen, and a few irrigations tied to key growth stages. For summer maize after wheat harvest, I will sow quickly, use improved seed, keep plant population uniform, and rely on fewer irrigations if rainfall is normal. I will use rotary tillage for the wheat season because it fits local residue handling and labor efficiency, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest to save time and conserve moisture. I will keep pesticide use targeted and limited, only enough to protect yield from the common local disease, weed, and insect pressure.
